For a **full-service upper-upscale hotel**, owners and developers usually begin with the following international brand universe. Exact positioning varies by country—what one operator calls “premium” may correspond to upper-upscale in another market.

### Core global shortlist

| Operator | Brands commonly considered | Typical fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott International** | **Marriott Hotels, Sheraton, Westin, Renaissance, Le Méridien** | Large urban hotels, resorts, convention/MICE properties and mixed-use developments |
| **Hilton** | **Hilton Hotels & Resorts, Curio Collection by Hilton**; sometimes **DoubleTree** or **Canopy** | Hilton for mainstream full service; Curio for distinctive independent-style hotels |
| **Hyatt** | **Hyatt Regency, Hyatt Centric, JdV by Hyatt**; occasionally **The Unbound Collection** | Regency for corporate/MICE; Centric and JdV for lifestyle assets |
| **IHG Hotels & Resorts** | **Crowne Plaza, Hotel Indigo, voco** | Crowne Plaza for corporate/MICE; Indigo for boutique lifestyle; voco for flexible conversions |
| **Accor** | **Pullman, Swissôtel, Mövenpick, MGallery Collection** | Particularly strong consideration in Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific |
| **Radisson Hotel Group** | **Radisson Blu**, sometimes **Radisson RED** or **Radisson Individuals** | Radisson Blu is a conventional upper-upscale candidate, especially in Europe, MEA and parts of Asia |
| **Wyndham Hotels & Resorts** | **Wyndham Grand, Registry Collection Hotels** | Upper-upscale hard-brand and soft-brand alternatives, respectively |

Hyatt itself identifies Marriott, Westin, Renaissance, Sheraton and Hilton as Hyatt Regency’s principal competitive set, which is a useful indication of the “core” global shortlist. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/hyattregency?utm_source=openai)) Marriott groups its principal full-service brands—including its collection options—within its premium/full-service development offering. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai))

### Practical shortlist by project type

**Conventional urban or business hotel**
- Marriott Hotels
- Sheraton
- Hilton Hotels & Resorts
- Hyatt Regency
- Crowne Plaza
- Pullman
- Radisson Blu
- Wyndham Grand

**Lifestyle or design-led hotel**
- Renaissance
- Le Méridien
- Hyatt Centric
- Hotel Indigo
- Canopy by Hilton
- MGallery
- Radisson RED

**Independent hotel seeking distribution without losing its identity**
- Autograph Collection
- Tribute Portfolio
- Curio Collection by Hilton
- JdV by Hyatt
- The Unbound Collection by Hyatt
- MGallery Collection
- Radisson Individuals
- Registry Collection Hotels

Curio, for example, operates as a global collection of individually distinctive hotels and currently has properties across dozens of countries; IHG positions Hotel Indigo as its globally expanding premium boutique brand. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/curio-collection-by-hilton-fact-sheet?utm_source=openai)) Wyndham explicitly positions Wyndham Grand and Registry Collection in the upper-upscale segment. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/brand/wyndham-grand/?utm_source=openai))

**Conversion or adaptive-reuse project**
- voco
- Curio Collection
- Autograph Collection
- Tribute Portfolio
- MGallery
- Radisson Individuals
- Registry Collection
- DoubleTree, depending on the target rate and local competitive set

IHG specifically markets voco as a flexible, lower-capital conversion proposition, with 137 hotels open and 113 in its pipeline as of March 31, 2026. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/voco-hotels?utm_source=openai))

### Brands often added regionally

- **Europe/Latin America:** NH Collection, Meliá, Barceló
- **Middle East/Africa:** Rotana, HUALUXE in selected markets, regional Accor brands
- **Asia-Pacific:** Pan Pacific, PARKROYAL COLLECTION, Dusit Thani, Avani, Grand Mercure
- **India/South Asia:** Taj/Vivanta, ITC/Welcomhotel, Lemon Tree’s higher-tier offerings
- **China:** domestic brands may be added depending on distribution, owner relations and management economics

### Most realistic first-round RFP list

For a broadly international, 200–400-key upper-upscale project, a balanced first-round list would often be:

1. Marriott Hotels or Sheraton  
2. Hilton Hotels & Resorts  
3. Hyatt Regency  
4. Crowne Plaza  
5. Pullman  
6. Radisson Blu  
7. Westin or Renaissance  
8. One lifestyle/soft-brand alternative—such as Curio, Autograph, Hotel Indigo, MGallery or Hyatt Centric  

Radisson describes Radisson Blu as Europe’s largest upper-upscale brand, while Accor places Pullman, Swissôtel and Mövenpick within its premium development portfolio. ([radissonhotels.com](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/corporate/development-opportunities/our-brands?utm_source=openai))

The final shortlist should be narrowed using **market availability and area-of-protection, brand contribution, projected ADR premium, loyalty penetration, key-money support, fee structure, technical-services requirements, PIP/capital cost and operator termination rights**—not brand prestige alone. Luxury brands such as JW Marriott, Conrad, Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, Fairmont and Sofitel normally belong in a separate comparison unless the site, room rates and development budget support genuine luxury positioning.
